In terms of other approaches to normalisation, I really have never come across anything else in optimisation, which is not to say they don't exist. The normalisation is done to let optimisers work with step sizes that make sense for all dimensions of the space. So if you are constraining MW and mT, for example, a step of 0.1 is tiny or huge, which complicates things. So typically you let all variables go [0..1] and the conversion is handled in the constraint and objective functions. If you want to "suggest" to the optimiser that e.g. a value approaching 1 would bad for variable x_1, then you'd add a penalty function of that variable to the objective.

So I won't plan on any architecture for different types of variables or normalisations (which would get quite heavy-set for what we need to day). But we can re-address it if it pops up.
